parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The graphs $y=\cot2x$ and $y=\sec x$ have exactly one intersection in the interval.
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: B1: Sketch a relevant graph, e.g. $y=\cot2x$ (alternative $\tan2x$ allowed). B1: Sketch a second relevant graph on the same axes, e.g. $y=\sec x$, and identify the single intersection/root. Total 2.

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: At the limit, $2x=\tan^{-1}(\cos x)$, hence $\tan2x=\cos x$ and $\cot2x=\sec x$.
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: B1: State $(1/2)\tan^{-1}(\cos x)=x$ and rearrange through $\tan2x=\cos x$ to $\cot2x=\sec x$; or reverse the steps from the equation to the iterative formula. Total 1.
